value.answer: Usually it comes down to timing and routine. Watch for sleepy cues like rubbing eyes, yawning, or getting fussy, and start the nap routine before he hits overtired, because an overtired kid often fights sleep harder. Keep the same steps every time: a quiet activity, a diaper change, a feed if it fits, into a dark room with white noise, then down drowsy but awake. Even if he doesn't fall asleep right away, lying quietly in his crib for a while still counts as rest. How long he can stay awake between naps depends a lot on his age, so if you tell me roughly how old he is I can help you pin down the timing.
